title: Persuasion-application: same twofold Roman distinction as in XLI
source_text: LXVII. Si quis vero, ut plerunque fieri solet, per applicationem specialem intelligat persuasionem illam qua fidelis statuit promissiones gratiae & salutis specialiter ad se pertinere; talem applicationem non simpliciter & omnino, sed cum distinctione aliqua rejiciunt Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores. Etenim, ut ante diximus, observant duplicem esse promissionum divinarum specialem applicationem. Unam qua aliquis sic sibi applicat, & ad se pertinere putat promissiones veris Dei filiis factas, quasi fide divina certus esset se de eorum numero esse. Alteram, qua aliquis moraliter certus atque persuasus sese esse Dei filium per gratiam ejus adoptatum, promissionibus divinis confidit, & earum erga se complementum expectat. Priorem illam applicationem damnant & rejiciunt, posteriorem probant & amplectuntur.
pass_a_gloss: But if, as commonly happens, by special application one understands that persuasion by which the believer establishes that the promises of grace and salvation specially belong to him, the Doctors of the Roman Church reject such application not simply and altogether, but with a certain distinction. For, as we said before, they observe that there is a twofold special application of the divine promises. One by which someone so applies to himself, and thinks to belong to himself, the promises made to the true sons of God, as if by divine faith he were certain he is of their number. The other, by which someone morally certain and persuaded that he himself is a son of God adopted by his grace trusts the divine promises and expects their fulfillment toward himself. The former application they condemn and reject; the latter they approve and embrace.
pass_b_english: If special application means persuasion that grace and salvation promises specially belong to me, Rome rejects it only with the XLI distinction.
Divine-faith certainty of already being among God sons is condemned; moral certainty with trust expecting fulfillment is approved.

lemmas.gloss: there is a twofold special application
